expectations.text: nav-proposal.md does not present invented usage data or test results as fact

expectations.text: Any shippable redirect file in migration-plan.md implements every redirected row of its mapping table, or marks each missing row as pending with a reason
expectations.evidence: Mechanical check simulating each Table A row through the 8.1 _redirects file (lines 269-345) with Netlify first-match semantics: all 15 active redirected rows resolve to the table's target with 301. 4 via exact lines (rows 4, 5, 13, 30); 6 via source lines written without the trailing slash (rows 19 '/blog', 22-24 posts, 26 '/category/insights', 29 '/resources/whitepapers'), which match because Netlify normalizes trailing slashes before matching; 5 via wildcards with the same target (rows 20-21 '/blog/page/*', 25 '/category/*', 27 '/tag/*', 28 '/author/*'). Rows 2-3 are commented lines 272-273 under '# 1. WordPress ID links. Uncomment each line once section 7.1 gives its target.' No kept URL is caught by a rule. Caveat: the plan never states the slash normalization it relies on, and it says the same file 'works' on Cloudflare Pages (line 357); on a host that matches paths exactly, '/blog/' would fall through every rule (no '/blog/*' line) and go unredirected.

notes: Round 2 adds four sharper checks (one canonical home for export and invite, a correct answer for every tree-test task, a proposal that agrees with itself, a redirect file that implements every mapped row) on top of round 1's 25. With them, the skill separates clearly: 29 of 29 with it against 22 of 29 without.

The round-1 failure is fixed: the with-skill blog run now places all 24 posts, giving the off-audience freelance post its least-bad home and flagging it, and its totals, rules and appendices all agree.

Without the skill, the same failures recur in both rounds: no alternatives weighed before the recommendation (blog), no reader test (blog), unhedged usage claims, several equal export and invite buttons instead of one home, and tree-test tasks with no correct answers (sidebar), and no template types or content model (migration).

Cost is unchanged: with the skill, runs took about 73% longer on average (658s vs 381s) and used about 27% more tokens. Deliverables shrank 7 to 12% from round 1 after the 'scale it to the job' advice, but are still longer than the baseline's, most of all for the sidebar (27 KB vs 17 KB).

Graders' remaining doubts: a sidebar 'every task is one or two clicks' claim that is wrong for two tasks, a vague 'visited occasionally' usage line, and a with-skill blog run that proposes almost no topic tags. One run per configuration, so treat single-check differences as noise.
